result: The authors developed a novel experimental system combining optogenetic stimulation (channelrhodopsin) with high-pressure freezing to capture synaptic vesicle dynamics at C. elegans neuromuscular junctions with millisecond temporal resolution (minimum ~20 ms interval between stimulation and freezing).
status_reasoning: All three reviewers explicitly praised this methodological advance as a 'tour de force' and 'remarkable.' Reviewer 1 states 'The combination of high-pressure freeze with temporal control of stimulation in a system that is amenable to genetic manipulations has been a long-sought goal.' Reviewer 2 calls it 'a modern version of the Heuser slam freeze protocol' and notes the approach 'will be referred to by experts in the field for many years to come.' The reviewers validate the technical capabilities without questioning the methodology.

result: Following stimulation, the authors observed exocytic intermediates (omega figures with wide necks) at 20 ms, with a significant reduction in docked vesicles (from 2.5±0.1 to 0.9±0.1 per profile, p<0.0001) but no change in tethered vesicles, indicating that only docked vesicles in the active zone undergo fusion.
status_reasoning: Reviewer 1 states 'The work described here contains a lovely and comprehensive description of exocytosis: the ability to capture classic omega-figures, docked and tethered vesicles provides a convincing framework.' Reviewer 2 describes the exocytosis findings as 'elegant' with 'convincing' interpretations. Reviewer 2 specifically notes they 'observe a loss of 10-20 docked SVs within 20ms' and accepts the conclusion that shallow pits 'correspond to evoked SV fusions.' No reviewer challenges these exocytic observations.

result: Docked vesicles fuse along a broad active zone extending from the dense projection to the adherens junctions, with exocytic pits distributed across the entire ~400 nm length of the active zone.
status_reasoning: Reviewer 2 explicitly accepts this finding, stating 'These structures are distributed throughout the length of the active zone (extending roughly 400 nm radially from the dense projection)' and notes 'The authors conclude that these shallow pits correspond to evoked SV fusions.' Reviewer 2 also confirms 'they observe a loss of 10-20 docked SVs within 20ms' distributed spatially. The reviewers do not challenge the spatial distribution of fusion events or the broad active zone conclusion.

result: Docked vesicles are replenished with a time constant of ~2.4 s, correlating with the slow phase of recovery from paired-pulse depression (τ=2.2 s), suggesting docked vesicles represent the morphological correlate of the readily releasable pool.
status_reasoning: Reviewer 1 explicitly validates this correlation: 'The close correspondence of the recovery from paired pulse depression and the docked pool re-population dynamics argues strongly that the authors are able to follow the correct physiological process.' Reviewer 2 states 'they observe a loss of 10-20 docked SVs within 20ms, which recovers in the next several seconds (tau ∼2 s)' and notes 'disappearance of endocytic intermediates correlates with the replenishment of docked SVs and with the refilling of the RRP.' This correlation is accepted as validating the approach.

result: Endocytosis occurs rapidly adjacent to the dense projection, with large vesicles/invaginations (~1.5x larger than synaptic vesicles) appearing and resolving within 50 ms, accounting for ~43% of vesicle recovery.
status_reasoning: Reviewer 1 acknowledges 'There is precedence for the larger vesicle formation near the dense projection as Heuser reported something similar' and states 'the speed of the reformation of the smaller endocytic events are nothing one would have predicted' but 'I see no flaws in the experiments or interpretations.' Reviewer 2 describes these findings as 'elegant' with 'convincing' interpretations, noting 'endocytic events occur in two zones: adjacent to either the dense projection or the adherens junction. Both forms of endocytosis occur rapidly, proximal and distal events peaking at 30ms and 300ms respectively.' The rapid timescale is accepted.

result: Endocytosis also occurs at adherens junctions with a time constant of ~1.4 s for pit resolution, accounting for ~57% of vesicle recovery.
status_reasoning: Reviewer 2 explicitly accepts this finding, stating 'endocytic events occur in two zones: adjacent to either the dense projection or the adherens junction' with 'distal events peaking at...300ms.' Reviewer 1 notes 'I see no flaws in the experiments or interpretations' regarding the endocytic findings. While Reviewer 3 questions whether these represent 'two mechanisms' versus different time courses, they do not challenge the observation of endocytosis at adherens junctions itself.

result: Dynamin is required for fast endocytosis, as demonstrated by temperature-sensitive dynamin mutants that stabilize large vesicles at restrictive temperature and show increased vesicle diameter after stimulation.
status_reasoning: Reviewer 2 accepts the dynamin data, noting 'their persistence is exaggerated by mutations inactivating dynamin' and 'it is shown that resolution of enlarged invaginations into vesicles requires dynamin activity.' Reviewer 1 expresses disappointment with 'the level of analysis of the ky dynamin mutant' but acknowledges 'there is really no equivalent to either the Drosophila shibire or mammalian k44A mutants in worms' and does not challenge the conclusion that dynamin is required. The finding is accepted despite limited analysis depth.

result: Synaptic vesicle endocytosis occurs on a millisecond timescale following a single physiological stimulus, with most vesicles retrieved rapidly, and this ultrafast endocytosis is unlikely to conform to current models (kiss-and-run or clathrin-mediated endocytosis).
status_reasoning: Reviewer 1 states 'This paper will be of high interest to the field' and 'one quickly gets the main message that endocytosis is not happening as one would have imagined. This result will be difficult to accept for some but I see no flaws in the experiments or interpretations.' Reviewer 2 finds the 'interpretations and conclusions are convincing' regarding the rapid endocytosis. Reviewer 3 states 'This is an excellent paper' and acknowledges it 'suggests that SV recycling may occur by mechanisms distinct from hitherto favored models.' While the interpretation challenges existing models, reviewers accept the data supporting ultrafast endocytosis.

result: Vesicles fuse throughout the active zone, but endocytosis is spatially segregated to the edges of the active zone (adjacent to dense projections and at adherens junctions).
status_reasoning: Reviewer 2 explicitly accepts this spatial organization, stating the data show 'endocytic events occur in two zones: adjacent to either the dense projection or the adherens junction' while fusion occurs 'throughout the length of the active zone.' Reviewer 1 notes 'I see no flaws in the experiments or interpretations' regarding the spatial findings. The spatial segregation of exocytosis and endocytosis is accepted by reviewers.

result: Only docked vesicles at the active zone can fuse after a single stimulus (~60% of docked vesicles), while tethered vesicles and ectopically docked vesicles in the perisynaptic zone do not undergo evoked fusion.
status_reasoning: Reviewer 2 accepts this finding, noting 'docked SVs are preferably consumed during single light stimuli, which release an equivalent of 4–6 SVs, i.e., about half of the docked SV pool.' Reviewer 1 validates the approach by stating 'The close correspondence of the recovery from paired pulse depression and the docked pool re-population dynamics argues strongly that the authors are able to follow the correct physiological process.' The selectivity of docked vesicle fusion is accepted.

result: Endocytic structures at dense projections show size heterogeneity, with some only slightly larger than single vesicles and others greater than twice the size of synaptic vesicles.
status_reasoning: Reviewer 2 describes the endocytic structures as 'shallow invaginations with diameters larger than SVs' and accepts the size measurements without challenge. Reviewer 1 notes precedence for 'larger vesicle formation near the dense projection' and sees 'no flaws in the experiments.' The size heterogeneity observation is implicitly accepted through the reviewers' acceptance of the overall endocytic findings.

result: Membrane balance calculations show that the amount of membrane exocytosed and endocytosed is roughly equal by 300 ms to 1 s after stimulation, with ~112-144 synaptic vesicle equivalents recovered through observed endocytic structures, suggesting all endocytic structures form rapidly within one second.
status_reasoning: Reviewer 1 explicitly validates this analysis: 'The fact that the analysis of the amount of exo matches the analysis for the amount of endo strongly suggests that the authors are tracking the right stuff here.' Reviewer 2 accepts the temporal analysis showing endocytic structures 'persist for ∼1 second after stimulation.' The membrane balance calculations are accepted as supporting evidence for rapid, complete endocytosis.

result: Clathrin coats can be preserved through the high-pressure freezing and freeze-substitution protocol using glutaraldehyde as primary fixative.
status_reasoning: Reviewer 3 asks 'Do these contain dynamin (i.e., by immunogold or by correlative SRLM/EM)?' regarding invaginations, implicitly accepting that the fixation can preserve protein structures. No reviewer challenges the technical claim about clathrin coat preservation. The methodological capability is accepted without dispute.

result: The invaginations and large vesicles observed post-stimulation represent endocytic rather than exocytic structures, based on their size (~1.5x larger than synaptic vesicles), timing, spatial location at active zone edges, and dependence on prior exocytosis.
status_reasoning: Reviewer 3 specifically requests 'further evidence that the invaginations seen post-stimulation (Figure 5) really do represent endocytic rather than exocytic structures' and asks 'Do these contain dynamin (i.e., by immunogold or by correlative SRLM/EM)?' This indicates the reviewer wants additional confirmation of the endocytic identity. While Reviewers 1 and 2 accept the interpretation, Reviewer 3's explicit request for more evidence indicates uncertainty about definitively distinguishing endocytic from exocytic structures based solely on morphology and timing.

result: There are two distinct mechanisms of ultrafast endocytosis occurring at different locations (dense projections vs. adherens junctions) with different kinetics (50 ms vs. 1.4 s).
status_reasoning: Reviewer 3 explicitly challenges this interpretation: 'Whether or not invaginations near dense projections vs. adherens junctions really represent two mechanisms of endocytosis in my opinion cannot be concluded from the data. What rather appears different is their time course.' Reviewer 3 also states 'This potential caveat should also be reflected in the title.' While the spatial and temporal differences are accepted, whether these represent two distinct mechanisms versus one mechanism with different kinetics is questioned. Reviewer 3 asks 'Is it conceivable that common structural determinants underlie ultrafast endocytosis at dense projections and AJs?'

result: Ultrafast endocytosis might require optogenetic stimulation methods and intact nervous system spatial constraints to be observed, potentially explaining why it wasn't detected in previous dissected preparations.
status_reasoning: Reviewer 1 raises a significant concern: 'one does not really have any idea what a "stimulus" means here. The ChIEF is meant to mimic the phasic type of stimuli one gets out of an action potential, but this system does not have action potentials. This is the only real weakness and prevents one from fully embracing these results.' This indicates uncertainty about whether the optogenetic stimulus truly mimics physiological conditions and whether the observed ultrafast endocytosis would occur under natural stimulation. The speculation about why this wasn't observed previously remains uncertain.
